basis_statement: Locators stay opaque and family-specific. Durable refs survive moves and copy-on-publish, while delivery handles require invocation-time context and route-bound security checks.

source_lineage.rationale: The customer experience contract freezes how current and historical artifacts expose preview and download surfaces.
Workspace attachments distinguish current artifact, historical artifact, storage backing, and download affordance.
Provenance graph traversal requires durable refs that survive derivative publication and replay.
Storage namespaces are internal object-store concerns and must not leak into durable API or UI locators.
Cache identity law already binds route, object, and delivery context separately.

notes: Durable refs are the long-lived contract surface for lineage and object identity.
A move, promote, or rehydrate operation may keep the same durable ref while storage or delivery state changes.
Targets express what should be shown or exported, not how bytes are fetched.
A historical artifact can retain a distinct lawful target set without replacing current defaults.
A resumable upload keeps the same `storage_ref` even when request version drifts.
Storage continuity does not imply current preview/download legality.
Delivery handles are disposable and must be rebound when the route, target, or access slice changes.
They exist to prevent stale tabs and broadened reuse.
Route tokens participate in delivery binding and cache partitioning but never become durable artifact truth.
Browser restoration may serialize route patterns or scene tokens, not full URLs.

selection_rules.statement: Default preview, download, and print targets must resolve from the current artifact only.
notes: Historical artifacts may have their own lawful targets, but only after explicit selection.
No fallback may infer a customer-visible target from `storage_ref`.

selection_rules.statement: Historical artifact targets remain selectable state, not ambient global defaults.
notes: Current and historical artifact meaning must stay visible in UI and API contracts.
Explicit history selection prevents stale target drift.

selection_rules.statement: A customer-safe derivative published from an internal-only source must mint a new target and a new delivery binding.
notes: The derivative may retain lineage to the source artifact ref.
The derivative must never expose the source storage namespace.

selection_rules.statement: Copy-on-publish may mint new storage and target families while preserving upstream durable artifact refs for lineage.
notes: Control truth decides which derivative is current.
Storage moves do not rewrite historical provenance.
